gaps.construct: groupby(data, type) and returning the class object T for later conversion
gaps.description: Scribe has no runtime type values. Replaced by a closed `choice Number` of the four accepted numeric kinds plus a `NumberKind` choice naming the result type; user-defined numeric types (any Python object with as_integer_ratio) cannot be accepted.

gaps.construct: duck-typed numeric data: _exact_ratio works on anything with as_integer_ratio
gaps.description: No interfaces or open polymorphism, so the set of supported numeric types is closed at declaration.

gaps.construct: dict partials keyed by denominator, set of types
gaps.description: The doc has List only: no Map or Set type. The dict becomes a list of records searched linearly (O(n) per item instead of O(1)), the set a list with an `is not in` guard.
The doc reads list elements with `item i of items` but has no form for writing one; `set item i of partials to ...` is invented by analogy with field mutation.

gaps.construct: None used as a dict key for the non-finite partial
gaps.description: Key-able missing values are not discussed and there is no map; the non-finite case is split into a separate `maybe` accumulator and a `Not_finite` variant of the exact ratio.

gaps.construct: reduce(_coerce, types, int) and sum(Fraction(n, d) for ...)
gaps.description: The doc has one comprehension form and a `sum of` in specs, but no fold/reduce; both become explicit accumulator loops.

gaps.construct: float, Fraction, Decimal, int mixed arithmetic
gaps.description: The doc names only Int, Nat and Money; whether Float, Fraction and Decimal exist, and how they combine under 'no implicit conversion', is not stated. Declared helper `fraction_from` does the explicit construction.
`expect` is shown only in headers and `assert` only in proof blocks; there is no shown form for a run-time assertion mid-body. `expect` is used inside the body.
The rule that allocating operations name an Allocator is followed in the header, but no example shows how `append` or list literals are tied to an allocator, so the growth sites cannot mention it.

gaps.construct: record construction `Partial(denominator=d, numerator=n)` and variant construction
gaps.description: Construction syntax appears only once (`an Order from cart and receipt with status Paid`); `a Partial with denominator d and numerator n` is a guess, and a field label that equals a bound variable name (`numerator numerator`) is hard to read and to parse.

gaps.construct: local var initialised to nothing or [] with no element type
gaps.description: The doc does not say whether a `var` can carry a type annotation; empty initial values leave the type to inference.
No tuples; a result record type SumResult is declared. Minor, but adds a type per multi-result function.

invented_syntax: set item i of partials to ... (element assignment)
a Partial with denominator d and numerator n (record construction)
Exact with value v (variant construction as an expression)
append kind to types on a local var list
expect used as a body statement
Float, Fraction, Decimal, Bool type names
notes: The function is algorithmically simple but leans on three things Scribe lacks: maps/sets, runtime type values, and duck typing, so the translation roughly doubles in length and changes complexity from O(n) to O(n*k). A standard Map and Set type with `item k of map` reading and a write form would remove most of the clumsiness. Reflection on type is a deliberate non-goal candidate, but then the doc should say that numeric-tower code uses a closed choice.
